transcript: Every now and then, we all need someone to hijack our Sunday afternoon. But in the delightful new comedy We Do The Same Thing Every Week by Robert Leverett, seemingly nothing can distract brother and sister Dick and Jane from their boredom and their pull toward the void. This is a zany, surreal, and absurd riff on The Cat in the Hat, and it's definitely a play that invites interpretation. Basically the Cat presents Dick and Jane a series of activities, having promised them fun, knowing the alternative is vacuum decay. Although this initial premise is somewhat simple, the themes that unfold are complex and kind of dark. Dick and Jane's relationship to their existence is both stringent and distant, and ultimately this is a play about repetition, mundaneness, and maybe even nihilism. The juxtaposition of philosophical language and a colorfully nostalgic aesthetic that invokes the set of Blue's Clues creates a funny and uncomfortable tension. It's a lot to unpack, but I thoroughly enjoy this. It's the kind of piece that’s specific, yet still perplexing, but in an intriguing way, not a frustrating one. And even though it's dense, there's no shortage of humor and surprises along the way, including music, puppetry, even trampolines. I thought it was great, and I found it unnervingly resonant — I don't know what that says about me. We Do The Same Thing Every Week is running at the A.R.T. Theatres through next Saturday, May 17th. With that, another program for my collection.
